items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: I hadn't heard of René. And I hadn't heard of Louis because I saw Louis.

ctx.x: Well when did you leave about?

In 1917. I arrived in Chicago January the 3rd, 1917. I was thirteen years old. And it wasn't long before I began to hear them talking about Louis Armstrong. My, at the time it was Joe Oliver. I'd seen them fellas bucking one another, him and Mutt. René, I hadn't heard of René. And I hadn't heard of Louis because I saw Louis. items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1973-09-07
items.q: I sat in there with that, I grabbed the trumbo one night, Morrissey here and played with him.

ctx.x: But what did you think about it? You said that René used to play the blues in these ladies?

Well René played in C Sharp. You mean C Sharp. C Sharp. Well that's the same thing. I sat in there with that, I grabbed the trumbo one night, Morrissey here and played with him. And I was feeling around him, you know. You were trying to find the trumbo? Feeling all around, trying to find the key. It was damn near old when I found the key, you understand what I'm talking about. Because I hadn't been used to playing.
Did you think René was a very good trumbo player?
